svg.text: CSEEE-21 / 5 V motor + Hall encoder / Nano ESP32 / example parts and values, untested
* Fit pull-up only if Hall output needs it.
Buffer protects 3.3 V logic from a 5 V signal.
C4 next to U2. Pin numbers assume SOT-23-5 / DBV.
U2 input accepts up to 5.5 V; output uses 3.3 V supply.
D5 / A0 remain available for heating.
D10 and D2 are board pin labels.
USB current budget must be checked
Measure the geared output shaft directly
RPM = 60 x pulse_frequency / 70. No further 10:1 correction.
At 1,000 RPM: approximately 1,167 pulses/s; period 857 us.
Measure pulse period; a 10 ms count has coarse 85.7 RPM steps.
Trial target: 800 RPM. Control tuning must use measured response.
Motor handout: approximately 1,000 RPM max at 5 V.
Confirm the older 1,500 RPM requirement with teaching staff.
VBUS supplies 5 V only when USB powered; do not add 6/12 V.
U2 / U3 are added interface parts; kit availability unconfirmed.
Example design. All grounds common; keep motor-current return separate from sensor wiring. C1 close to assembly supply.
Gate driver pin 3 NC. Motor starting/stall current and USB/VBUS capacity are not supplied; verify before energising.
